entries.issuing_body: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York
entries.title: SDNY denies Novig's preliminary injunction, holding its sports event contracts are not swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act
entries.facts: In Ludlow Exchange, LLC d/b/a Novig v. Letitia James, No. 1:26-cv-06676-CM (S.D.N.Y.), Judge McMahon issued a 35-page Opinion and Order denying the plaintiff's motion for a preliminary injunction, docketed as ECF No. 73 and stamped filed November 10, 2026. The opinion states that the court "concludes that Novig's contracts are not 'swaps' within the meaning of the Commodities Exchange Act, so New York can apply its" gambling and sports-wagering laws, and that the contracts "bear more than a passing resemblance to sports betting." On the question whether the contracts depend on an event or contingency, the opinion states that the court "reaches the same conclusion as the Third and Sixth Circuits." The order concludes: "Accordingly, Plaintiffs motion for a preliminary injunction is denied." The named defendants are the New York Attorney General and members of the New York State Gaming Commission, each sued in an official capacity. Novig filed the suit on August 5, 2026.
entries.source_label: Opinion and Order (ECF No. 73), Ludlow Exchange LLC v. James, No. 1:26-cv-06676 (S.D.N.Y. Nov. 10, 2026) - court PDF, copy hosted by Sports Betting Dime

entries.title: KalshiEX rule change on perpetual security futures listing standards publishes at 91 FR 72935, comments due December 3, 2026
entries.facts: Federal Register document 2026-22958, published November 12, 2026 at 91 FR 72935, is the SEC's notice "Self-Regulatory Organizations; KalshiEX LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change Relating to Listing Standards for Security Futures Products," Release No. 34-106841, File No. SR-KALSHIEX-2026-03, dated November 6, 2026 and filed by KalshiEX on November 4, 2026. The notice states that comments "should be submitted on or before December 3, 2026" and that "The proposed rule change will become effective on November 19, 2026." The filing is made under Section 19(b)(7) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 19b-7. The change amends Rule 14.3 listing criteria for Perpetual Security Futures Products: proposed Rule 14.3(c) provides that where an underlying security has been listed for trading for less than one month it must have had "a trading volume (in all markets in which it is traded) of at least 2,400,000 shares" since its initial public offering day; proposed Rule 14.3(d) would waive the five-day three-dollar closing-price criterion for covered securities during the first three business days after an initial public offering where the issuer's market capitalization based on the offering price is at least 3,000,000,000 dollars, with listing permitted from the second business day following the offering day. The notice states that the text of the rule change is provided in Exhibit 4 to the filing.

entries.issuing_body: U.S. House Committee on Education and the Workforce
entries.title: House subcommittee holds hearing on sports gambling on college campuses with the chair of the Massachusetts Gaming Commission among the witnesses
entries.facts: The Subcommittee on Higher Education and Workforce Development of the U.S. House Committee on Education and the Workforce held a hearing titled "The Rise of Sports Gambling on College Campuses" on November 11, 2026 at 10:15 AM in 2175 Rayburn Office Building. The committee's event page lists four witnesses: Dr. Lindsey Mortenson, Chief Mental Health Officer, Clinical Assistant Professor of Psychiatry and Executive Director of University Health and Counseling at the University of Michigan; Dr. Daniel Durkin, Associate Professor at the University of Mississippi; Mr. Jordan Maynard, Chair of the Massachusetts Gaming Commission; and Ms. Cindy Clouner, Managing Director of the Higher Education Center for Alcohol and Drug Misuse Prevention and Recovery at The Ohio State University. The page links written testimony for each witness, an opening statement by Representative Michael Baumgartner, and video of the hearing.
entries.source_label: U.S. House Committee on Education and the Workforce, hearing page (Nov. 11, 2026)
